about.title: Personal Injury Help in Walnut, California
about.longDescription: Walnut sits in a quiet corner of Los Angeles County, but its roads still see a steady share of collisions. Public records show 37 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, leaving 44 people hurt — thankfully with no traffic deaths reported. Corridors like Grand Avenue, Amar Road, Lemon Avenue, and La Puente Road carry much of the city's traffic, and that volume shows up in the crash counts. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that helps injured people in Walnut connect with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't handle your case ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. California law gives most injury victims two years from the date of the incident to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require action in as little as six months. Getting matched early with the right attorney can help protect your options while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Injured Walnut Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two-Year Filing Window
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. That window can shrink to as little as six months for claims against a government entity, so early action matters.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible for the incident. Your recovery is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This matters when injuries affect daily life long after medical bills are paid.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to get legal help. They only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Walnut?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the incident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle or public property, the window can be as short as six months. It's best to get matched with an attorney early so important deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Walnut?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors like Grand Avenue, Amar Road, Lemon Avenue, and La Puente Road, with Wednesdays between 3 and 5 p.m. showing more reported crashes than other times. These are simply public-record counts of where and when collisions have been reported, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your compensation would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but you can still pursue a claim.

items.question: Is there a cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys — we are not a law firm and we don't charge for the connection. If you're matched with an attorney, they typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: How much is my case worth?
items.answer: There's no way to give a dollar figure without a full review of your medical records, expenses, and the circumstances of your injury. An independent attorney can evaluate the specifics of your situation and explain your options after learning the details.
